label: Intermediate
blurb: The vocabulary of getting things done — the offices you have to visit, the paperwork you get handed, and the words that come up when you talk to parents.
blurbZh: 把事情辦好會用到的詞彙：各處室、要簽要交的文件，以及跟家長溝通時聽到的說法。

questions.q: A homeroom teacher asks you to write a note in a student's 聯絡簿. This is —
questions.why: 聯絡簿 (liánluòbù) goes home in the schoolbag every day. Teachers write homework and short notes in it; parents sign to confirm they've read it.

questions.q: The office asks if you can 代課 tomorrow morning. They want you to —
questions.why: 代課 (dàikè) = to substitute-teach. The person doing it is a 代課老師 (dàikè lǎoshī), a substitute teacher.

questions.q: You need to be away on Friday. You tell the office 我禮拜五要 (wǒ lǐbàiwǔ yào)—
questions.why: 請假 (qǐngjià) = to request leave. Common types: 病假 (bìngjià) sick leave, 事假 (shìjià) personal leave, 公假 (gōngjià) official leave.

questions.q: Questions about your timetable and textbooks are handled by the —
questions.why: 教務處 (jiàowùchù) = academic affairs — timetables, textbooks, exams. 學務處 handles student life, 總務處 the building and budget.

questions.q: A student has a discipline or safety issue. The office that handles it is —
questions.why: 學務處 (xuéwùchù) = student affairs — discipline, health, clubs, safety. It is the office you'll deal with most outside your own classes.

questions.q: You're invited to a 班親會 on Friday evening. This is —
opts: a parent–teacher meeting for one class
questions.why: 班親會 (bānqīnhuì) is the class-level parent meeting run by the homeroom teacher. FETs are often asked to say a few words.

questions.q: A colleague says 下禮拜段考. Next week there will be —
questions.why: 段考 (duànkǎo) is the periodic term exam — usually two or three per semester. 期末考 (qímòkǎo) is the final one.

questions.q: The calendar marks next Monday as 補假. This means —
opts: a make-up day off for a holiday you worked
questions.why: 補假 (bǔjià) is the compensating day off. Its partner is 補班 (bǔbān) — a Saturday you have to work to bridge a long weekend.

questions.q: A student proudly says they are this week's 值日生. They are —
opts: the student on duty for classroom chores
a hall monitor for the whole school
the top scorer on the last exam
questions.why: 值日生 (zhírìshēng) is the student on rotating duty — wiping the board, turning off lights, fetching the lunch cart.

questions.q: The 家長會 is sponsoring the sports day prizes. This group is —
questions.why: 家長會 (jiāzhǎnghuì) is the school-wide parent association. Don't confuse it with 班親會, the meeting for a single class.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. Your colleague is telling you that on Saturday there is —
questions.why: 研習 (yánxí) = an in-service training session or workshop. Teachers must accumulate 研習時數 (yánxí shíshù), training hours, each year.

questions.q: A teacher asks 我們調課好嗎？They are proposing to —
opts: swap class periods with each other
questions.why: 調課 (tiáokè) = to swap or reschedule periods between teachers. Different from 代課 (dàikè), where someone covers for you.

questions.q: You need to interrupt two colleagues who are talking. You open with —
questions.why: 不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi) works as 'excuse me' and as a light apology. It is softer than 對不起, which is a real apology.

questions.q: You tell the office 我要影印三十份. You need —
questions.why: 影印 (yǐngyìn) = to photocopy; 份 (fèn) is the measure word for copies or sets. The machine itself is the 影印機 (yǐngyìnjī).

questions.py: wǒ jīntiān yǒu sì jié kè
questions.q: Your colleague says 我今天有四節課. The measure word 節 is counting —
questions.why: 節 (jié) counts class periods: 一節課 = one period. For classes as groups use 班 (bān), and for people use 位 (wèi) politely.

questions.q: Parents refer to you as their child's 導師. This word means —
questions.why: 導師 (dǎoshī), often shortened to 班導 (bāndǎo), is the homeroom teacher responsible for one class's daily life.

questions.q: The newsletter says 校慶 is next month. The school is preparing for —
questions.why: 校慶 (xiàoqìng) is the founding anniversary — usually a big day with performances, sports, and alumni visiting.

questions.q: You are asked to prepare a 學習單 for your lesson. This is —
opts: a lesson plan for the principal
questions.why: 學習單 (xuéxídān) is the worksheet students fill in during or after an activity. 教案 (jiào'àn) is the lesson plan itself.

questions.q: A clerk hands you a form and says 麻煩您核章. They need you to —
opts: sign or stamp it to approve it
questions.why: 核章 (hézhāng) = to sign off with your seal or signature. Taiwanese paperwork moves by collecting 章 (zhāng), personal stamps, down a chain.

questions.q: Staff start discussing 期末 preparations. They mean —
opts: the start of a new school year
questions.why: 期末 (qímò) = end of term, with 期末考 (finals) and 結業式 (jiéyèshì, closing ceremony). Its opposite is 期初 (qíchū).

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. At three o'clock in the meeting room there will be —
questions.why: 開會 (kāihuì) = to hold a meeting. 會議室 (huìyìshì) is the meeting room; the weekly staff meeting is 校務會議 (xiàowù huìyì).

questions.q: A student who missed the exam will have a 補考. This is —
questions.why: 補考 (bǔkǎo) = make-up exam. The 補 (bǔ) prefix means 'to make up' — you'll also meet 補課 (make-up class) and 補假 (make-up day off).

questions.py: jīntiān yǒu liǎng wèi jiāzhǎng lái
questions.q: Someone says 今天有兩位家長來. Why 位 (wèi) rather than 個 (gè)?
opts: 位 (wèi) is only used for numbers over ten
位 (wèi) is the polite measure word for people
位 (wèi) means the parents are seated
questions.why: 位 (wèi) is the respectful measure word for people — 一位老師, 兩位家長. 個 (gè) is neutral and can sound blunt for guests.

questions.q: You tell the class 我們來分組. You are asking them to —
questions.why: 分組 (fēnzǔ) = to divide into groups; a group is a 組 (zǔ). 小組討論 (xiǎozǔ tǎolùn) is group discussion.

questions.q: You need five more minutes before going to the office. You say —
opts: 我等一下再過去 (wǒ děng yíxià zài guòqù)
我先下班了 (wǒ xiān xiàbān le)
questions.why: 等一下 (děng yíxià) = in a moment / hold on. 我等一下再過去 means 'I'll come over in a bit' — polite and very common.

questions.q: A student is struggling emotionally. The office that supports them is the —
questions.why: 輔導室 (fǔdǎoshì) is the counselling office. If you notice a student in difficulty, telling the 導師 and 輔導室 is the right first step.

questions.q: The schedule shows 防災演練 on Wednesday. You should expect —
questions.why: 防災演練 (fángzāi yǎnliàn) = disaster drill. In Taiwan this usually means 地震 (dìzhèn, earthquake) — duck, cover, hold, then evacuate to the playground.

questions.q: A student says they joined 熱舞社 this semester. 社 here refers to —
questions.why: 社 (shè) is short for 社團 (shètuán), a student club. 熱舞社 is the street-dance club; 英語社 would be the English club.

questions.q: A colleague ends a request with 拜託你了. The tone is —
opts: warm and pleading — 'I'm counting on you'
questions.why: 拜託 (bàituō) = please / I'm counting on you. Among colleagues it's friendly; it is stronger and warmer than 麻煩你.

questions.q: Parents will receive the 成績單 at the end of term. This is —
questions.why: 成績單 (chéngjīdān) = report card or transcript. 成績 (chéngjī) alone means grades or results.

questions.q: A broken air conditioner in your classroom should be reported to the —
questions.why: 總務處 (zǒngwùchù) = general affairs — buildings, equipment, purchasing, repairs. Your first stop for anything physically broken.

questions.q: Questions about your contract and leave records go to the —
questions.why: 人事室 (rénshìshì) = personnel office — contracts, leave records, insurance, staff paperwork.

questions.q: The 會計室 handles —
questions.why: 會計室 (kuàijìshì) = accounting office. Your 核銷 (expense claim) paperwork ends up here.

questions.q: 教務主任 is the —
questions.why: 主任 (zhǔrèn) = director of a department. Below them are 組長 (zǔzhǎng), section heads.

questions.q: A 組長 is a —
questions.why: 組長 (zǔzhǎng) heads a section such as 教學組 or 訓育組. In practice they handle most of the day-to-day paperwork you'll meet.

questions.q: The 工友 at your school —
questions.why: 工友 (gōngyǒu) is the general handyman/caretaker. If a door sticks or a table needs moving, they are the person.

questions.q: A 志工 helping at the school gate is a —
questions.why: 志工 (zhìgōng) = volunteer, often parents. The morning traffic-duty ones are the 導護志工 (dǎohù zhìgōng).

questions.q: An 實習老師 in your class is a —
questions.why: 實習老師 (shíxí lǎoshī) = trainee teacher doing their practicum. My Culture Connect's FET placements use the same word 實習.

questions.q: A 通知單 sent home is a —
questions.why: 通知單 (tōngzhīdān) = notification slip. Parents usually sign the attached 回條 (huítiáo) and return it.

questions.q: The 回條 at the bottom of a notice is the —
opts: reply slip parents sign and return
questions.why: 回條 (huítiáo) is the tear-off reply slip. Chasing unreturned 回條 is a standard homeroom chore.

questions.q: A 請假單 is a —
questions.why: 請假單 (qǐngjiàdān) = leave form. Most schools now file it online, but the word stayed.

questions.q: 病假 is leave taken —
questions.why: 病假 (bìngjià) = sick leave. The set also has 事假 (personal), 公假 (official) and 婚假 (marriage leave).

questions.q: You attend a county workshop during school hours. This is recorded as —
questions.why: 公假 (gōngjià) = official leave for school business. It does not come out of your personal leave allowance.

questions.q: 事假 is leave for —
questions.why: 事假 (shìjià) = personal leave. Usually unpaid or deducted, so colleagues use it sparingly.

questions.q: A Saturday marked 補班 means —
opts: a working day to bridge a long weekend
questions.why: 補班 (bǔbān) is a make-up work day. Taiwan shifts a weekday holiday and pays it back with a Saturday of school.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. Your colleague this afternoon has —
questions.why: 下午 (xiàwǔ) = afternoon; 上午 (shàngwǔ) = morning. 開會 is to attend or hold a meeting.

questions.q: 校務會議 is the —
questions.why: 校務會議 (xiàowù huìyì) is the full staff meeting that approves school-wide decisions, held a few times a semester.

questions.q: A 領域會議 brings together teachers of —
questions.why: 領域 (lǐngyù) = curriculum domain. The 英語領域會議 is where English teachers plan together — the one FETs attend.

questions.q: A teacher on 導護 duty is —
opts: on traffic and safety duty at the gate
questions.why: 導護 (dǎohù) is the morning and afternoon safety duty — helping students cross the road at the school gate.

questions.q: 校外教學 is a —
questions.why: 校外教學 (xiàowài jiàoxué) = off-campus learning, i.e. a field trip. Also called 戶外教育 (hùwài jiàoyù).

questions.q: A 園遊會 is a —
questions.why: 園遊會 (yuányóuhuì) is the school fair, often run with 校慶. Classes set up food and game stalls.

questions.q: 畢業典禮 is the —
questions.why: 畢業典禮 (bìyè diǎnlǐ) = graduation ceremony, held in June. 典禮 (diǎnlǐ) is the general word for a formal ceremony.

questions.q: 結業式 marks the —
questions.why: 結業式 (jiéyèshì) is the closing assembly at the end of a semester — awards, reminders, and holiday safety talks.

questions.py: zhè fèn yào yǐngyìn jǐ fèn?
questions.q: 🔊 Listen. You are being asked —
opts: How many copies of this do you need?
questions.why: 份 (fèn) is the measure word for copies and sets. 幾份 asks how many.

questions.q: 一張紙 uses 張 because 張 counts —
questions.why: 張 (zhāng) counts flat things — paper, tickets, tables, photos. 一張紙, 兩張桌子, 三張照片.

questions.q: Which measure word goes with 書?
questions.why: 本 (běn) counts bound volumes — 一本書, 兩本課本, 三本聯絡簿.

questions.q: 一台電腦 uses 台 because 台 counts —
questions.why: 台 (tái) counts machines — 一台電腦, 一台影印機, 一台車.

questions.q: 一間教室 uses 間 because 間 counts —
questions.why: 間 (jiān) counts rooms — 一間教室, 兩間辦公室. For whole buildings use 棟 (dòng).

questions.q: You ask students to 訂正 their work. They should —
questions.why: 訂正 (dìngzhèng) = to correct errors. Taiwanese students are expected to 訂正 every wrong answer, not just read the mark.

questions.q: 考卷 is the —
questions.why: 考卷 (kǎojuàn) = test paper. 改考卷 (gǎi kǎojuàn) is to mark them and 發考卷 to hand them back.

questions.q: 及格 means to —
questions.why: 及格 (jígé) = to reach the pass mark, usually 60. 不及格 (bù jígé) is a fail, and leads to a 補考.

questions.q: You ask a student to 上台. They should —
questions.why: 上台 (shàngtái) = go up on stage / to the front. 上台報告 (shàngtái bàogào) is to present to the class.

questions.q: In a classroom, 報告 most often means a —
questions.why: 報告 (bàogào) = report or presentation. A student standing at the door also says 報告 to ask permission to enter.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. You are being asked to —
questions.why: 簽名 (qiānmíng) = to sign. 蓋章 (gàizhāng) is to stamp with a seal — often both are needed.

questions.q: 蓋章 means to —
questions.why: 蓋章 (gàizhāng) = apply your 印章 (yìnzhāng), the personal seal that functions like a signature in Taiwanese paperwork.

questions.q: 報帳 is the process of —
opts: submitting receipts to claim money back
questions.why: 報帳 (bàozhàng) = to file an expense claim. Keep the 發票 (fāpiào, official receipt) or the claim will be refused.

questions.q: You must keep the 發票 to claim expenses. This is the —
questions.why: 發票 (fāpiào) is Taiwan's government-issued receipt. Ask for 統編 (company tax number) when buying for school.

questions.q: 經費 refers to —
questions.why: 經費 (jīngfèi) = funds allocated to a project. 經費不足 (jīngfèi bùzú) means the budget won't stretch.

questions.q: A 教案 is a —
questions.why: 教案 (jiào'àn) = lesson plan. Distinct from the 學習單 (xuéxídān), the worksheet students actually fill in.

questions.q: 教學進度 refers to the —
opts: teaching schedule / pace through the syllabus
questions.why: 教學進度 (jiàoxué jìndù) is how far through the curriculum you should be by a given week — submitted at the start of term.

questions.q: A 專科教室 is a —
questions.why: 專科教室 (zhuānkē jiàoshì) = specialist room — music, art, science, computing. Booked in advance through the office.

questions.q: 活動中心 is the —
questions.why: 活動中心 (huódòng zhōngxīn) is the covered multi-purpose hall used for assembly, PE on rainy days, and performances.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. You are being told that something is —
opts: due to be handed in next week
questions.why: 交 (jiāo) = to hand in or submit. 期限 (qíxiàn) is the deadline; 逾期 (yúqí) means overdue.

questions.q: A 中央廚房 —
questions.why: 中央廚房 (zhōngyāng chúfáng) is a central kitchen cooking 營養午餐 for its own school and neighbouring ones.

questions.q: 營養午餐 is —
questions.why: 營養午餐 (yíngyǎng wǔcān) is the government-standard school lunch every Taiwanese student eats in the classroom.

questions.q: The 午餐秘書 is the staff member who —
questions.why: 午餐秘書 (wǔcān mìshū) handles menus, suppliers and lunch fees — a real job title in Taiwanese schools.

questions.q: 健康檢查 at school is a —
questions.why: 健康檢查 (jiànkāng jiǎnchá) is the annual student health screening — height, weight, eyesight, teeth.

questions.q: 視力檢查 tests students' —
questions.why: 視力 (shìlì) = eyesight. Taiwanese schools track it closely because of high myopia rates.

questions.q: A colleague is juggling a stack of books. You offer —
questions.why: 我幫你 (wǒ bāng nǐ) = let me help you. 幫忙 (bāngmáng) is the noun: 需要幫忙嗎？— need a hand?

questions.q: 交給我 tells a colleague —
questions.why: 交給我 (jiāo gěi wǒ) = leave it with me, I'll handle it. Confident and reassuring among colleagues.

questions.q: 班級經營 refers to —
questions.why: 班級經營 (bānjí jīngyíng) covers rules, routines and relationships in a class — a standard topic in teacher training.

questions.q: 建立常規 in a classroom means establishing —
questions.why: 常規 (chángguī) = routine, standard practice. 常規不好 is the polite way to say a class is hard to settle.

questions.q: 獎勵 is a system of —
questions.why: 獎勵 (jiǎnglì) = reward or incentive. 獎勵制度 (jiǎnglì zhìdù) is a reward system — stickers, points, prizes.

questions.q: 處罰 means —
questions.why: 處罰 (chǔfá) = punishment. Corporal punishment is illegal in Taiwan; schools use 愛的教育 and loss of privileges instead.

questions.q: A student receiving 輔導 is getting —
questions.why: 輔導 (fǔdǎo) = guidance or counselling, run by the 輔導室. It also means academic remediation.

questions.q: 補救教學 provides —
opts: remedial teaching for students who are behind
questions.why: 補救教學 (bǔjiù jiàoxué) is the government-funded remedial programme, often after school. FETs are sometimes asked to help.

questions.q: A student described as a 個案 is —
opts: an individual case needing special attention
questions.why: 個案 (gè'àn) = individual case. Used discreetly for students under counselling or social-work support.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. You are being told that —
opts: a parent has arrived at the gate
a parent has sent a letter
questions.why: 打電話 (dǎ diànhuà) = to make a phone call. 來 marks the call as incoming.

questions.q: 跟家長溝通 means to —
questions.why: 溝通 (gōutōng) = to communicate, especially to talk something through. 溝通不良 means a misunderstanding.

questions.q: A parent 反映 a problem to the school. They have —
questions.why: 反映 (fǎnyìng) = to bring an issue to someone's attention. Neutral — it isn't necessarily a complaint.

questions.q: 家庭訪問 is a —
questions.why: 家庭訪問 (jiātíng fǎngwèn), shortened to 家訪, is still common in rural Changhua for students needing support.

questions.q: A 親師座談會 is a —
questions.why: 親師座談會 (qīnshī zuòtánhuì) is the parent–teacher conference, usually early in each semester. 親師 = parents and teachers.

questions.q: 新生 refers to —
opts: new students starting at the school
questions.why: 新生 (xīnshēng) = new intake. 新生訓練 (xīnshēng xùnliàn) is the orientation programme before term starts.

questions.q: A 轉學生 has —
questions.why: 轉學生 (zhuǎnxuéshēng) = transfer student. 轉出 is transferring out, 轉入 transferring in.

questions.q: 缺席 means —
questions.why: 缺席 (quēxí) = absent. 出席 (chūxí) is present or attending; 遲到 (chídào) is late.

questions.q: 遲到 means to —
questions.why: 遲到 (chídào) = to be late. 早退 (zǎotuì) is to leave early — the two often appear together on attendance records.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. The person being described today is —
questions.why: 請病假 (qǐng bìngjià) = to take sick leave. 請 here means 'to apply for', not 'please'.

questions.q: A 代理教師 is a —
opts: contract teacher covering a post for a year
questions.why: 代理教師 (dàilǐ jiàoshī) fills a post on a yearly contract. Different from 代課老師, who covers individual lessons.

questions.q: A 正式老師 is a —
questions.why: 正式老師 (zhèngshì lǎoshī) holds a permanent public-school appointment, won through the 教師甄試 examination.

questions.q: 教師甄試 is the —
opts: competitive examination for permanent teaching posts
questions.why: 教師甄試 (jiàoshī zhēnshì) is the fiercely competitive recruitment exam. Colleagues preparing for it will be very busy in spring.

questions.q: A 研習證明 is a —
questions.why: 研習證明 (yánxí zhèngmíng) proves you attended a workshop and logs the hours toward your 研習時數.

questions.q: 進修 refers to —
questions.why: 進修 (jìnxiū) = further study. Many Taiwanese teachers do a part-time master's — 在職進修 (zàizhí jìnxiū).

questions.py: zhè jié kè wǒ yào jiè jiàoshì
questions.q: 🔊 Listen. For this period the speaker wants to —
questions.why: 借教室 (jiè jiàoshì) = to book/borrow a room. 節 (jié) is the measure word for a class period.

questions.q: 排課 is the process of —
questions.why: 排課 (páikè) = timetabling, done by 教務處 before each semester. 課表 (kèbiǎo) is the resulting timetable.

questions.q: 課表 is your —
questions.why: 課表 (kèbiǎo) = timetable. Ask for yours in your first week: 我可以看我的課表嗎？

questions.q: 鐘點費 is payment —
questions.why: 鐘點費 (zhōngdiǎnfèi) = hourly rate, paid for extra classes, camps and after-school programmes.

questions.q: 加班 means to —
questions.why: 加班 (jiābān) = overtime. 加班費 (jiābānfèi) is overtime pay — different from 鐘點費 for teaching.

questions.q: 值班 during the holidays means —
opts: being on duty at school on a rota
questions.why: 值班 (zhíbān) = to be on duty. Schools keep a skeleton rota during 寒假 and 暑假.

questions.q: A 公文 arriving from the Education Bureau is an —
questions.why: 公文 (gōngwén) = official correspondence. It comes with a deadline and usually needs someone to 承辦 (handle) it.

questions.q: A 公告 on the noticeboard is a —
questions.why: 公告 (gōnggào) = notice or announcement, posted physically or on the school website.

questions.zh: 麻煩你下午三點到辦公室
questions.py: máfan nǐ xiàwǔ sān diǎn dào bàngōngshì
questions.q: 🔊 Listen. You are asked to go to the office —
questions.why: 三點 (sān diǎn) = three o'clock; 下午三點 = 3pm. 到 (dào) here means 'come to' a place.

questions.q: 簽到 means to —
questions.why: 簽到 (qiāndào) = to sign in. 簽退 (qiāntuì) is signing out at the end of the day.

questions.q: 打卡 at school means to —
questions.why: 打卡 (dǎkǎ) = to clock in or out. Many schools use a card reader by the office door.

questions.q: 薪水 is your —
questions.why: 薪水 (xīnshuǐ) = salary. 勞健保 (láojiànbǎo) is the labour and health insurance deducted from it.

questions.q: 勞健保 refers to —
questions.why: 勞健保 (láojiànbǎo) bundles 勞保 (labour insurance) and 健保 (national health insurance). Your 健保卡 gets you cheap clinic visits.

questions.q: You take your 健保卡 when you —
questions.why: 健保卡 (jiànbǎokǎ) is the national health insurance card. Carry it — a clinic visit costs a few hundred NT with it.

questions.py: qǐng nǐ xiān qiānmíng zài gàizhāng
questions.q: 🔊 Listen. You are asked to sign and then —
questions.why: 先…再… (xiān … zài …) = first … then …. A very common instruction pattern in the office.

questions.q: An 影本 of your passport is a —
questions.why: 影本 (yǐngběn) = photocopy. 正本 (zhèngběn) is the original — offices often ask to see both.

questions.q: 正本 means the —
questions.why: 正本 (zhèngběn) = original. 驗正本、留影本 (check the original, keep the copy) is standard office practice.

questions.q: Your 居留證 is your —
questions.why: 居留證 (jūliúzhèng) is the ARC. 人事室 will ask for a 影本 of it more than once.

questions.q: A 工作證 is a —
questions.why: 工作證 (gōngzuòzhèng) = work permit or staff ID card. Keep it with your 居留證 for school paperwork.

questions.q: Asked about a rule you don't know, the polite reply is —
opts: 我不太清楚 (wǒ bú tài qīngchǔ)
questions.why: 我不太清楚 (wǒ bú tài qīngchǔ) = I'm not quite sure. Softer and more professional than a flat 我不知道.

questions.q: 我再確認一下 tells a colleague you will —
opts: double-check and get back to them
questions.why: 確認 (quèrèn) = to confirm or verify. 我再確認一下 buys time politely and is very common at work.

questions.q: 提醒 means to —
questions.why: 提醒 (tíxǐng) = to remind. 提醒一下 (tíxǐng yíxià) softens a nudge: 'just a reminder…'

questions.q: 通知 as a verb means to —
questions.why: 通知 (tōngzhī) = to notify. As a noun it is the notice itself; the slip sent home is the 通知單.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. The speaker will —
questions.why: 過去 (guòqù) = to go over there. 過來 (guòlái) is to come over here — direction is from the speaker's side.

questions.q: 順便 means —
opts: while you're at it / on the way
questions.why: 順便 (shùnbiàn) = as a convenient extra. 順便幫我拿一下 = grab it for me while you're there.

questions.q: 盡量 means —
opts: as much as possible / do your best
questions.why: 盡量 (jǐnliàng) = do what you can. 盡量早一點 = as early as you can manage — a soft, non-binding request.

questions.q: A 臨時 change to the timetable is —
questions.why: 臨時 (línshí) = at short notice, temporary. 臨時有事 (línshí yǒu shì) means something has just come up.

questions.q: Declining an invitation politely, you say —
opts: 不好意思，我有事 (bù hǎoyìsi, wǒ yǒu shì)
questions.why: 有事 (yǒu shì) = to have something on. Paired with 不好意思 it is the standard, face-saving way to decline.

questions.q: 教學觀摩 is a lesson that —
questions.why: 教學觀摩 (jiàoxué guānmó) is an open demonstration lesson for professional sharing — not an appraisal.

questions.q: 公開授課 is now a yearly requirement for Taiwanese teachers. It means —
opts: teaching one lesson open to observers
questions.why: 公開授課 (gōngkāi shòukè) requires each teacher to open one lesson a year, with 共同備課 before and 議課 after.

questions.q: 議課 takes place —
opts: after an observed lesson, to discuss it
questions.why: 議課 (yìkè) is the post-lesson discussion. The full cycle is 共備 (co-plan) → 觀課 (observe) → 議課 (discuss).

questions.q: 觀課 means to —
questions.why: 觀課 (guānkè) = lesson observation. As an FET you will be invited to both observe and be observed.

questions.q: 共備 (gòngbèi) is short for 共同備課, which means —
questions.why: 共備 (gòngbèi) is collaborative lesson planning — the heart of co-teaching with your Taiwanese partner teacher.

questions.q: 協同教學 describes —
opts: two teachers teaching a class together
teaching alone with an assistant present
questions.why: 協同教學 (xiétóng jiàoxué) = co-teaching. The standard model for FETs paired with a local English teacher.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. Next week you and your colleague will —
questions.why: 下禮拜 (xià lǐbài) = next week; 上禮拜 (shàng lǐbài) = last week; 這禮拜 = this week.

questions.q: 教學資源 refers to —
questions.why: 教學資源 (jiàoxué zīyuán) covers everything you teach with — books, flashcards, digital materials, the resource centre's loans.

questions.q: An 英語村 is a —
opts: village twinned with an English town
questions.why: 英語村 (yīngyǔ cūn) is an English Village — themed rooms (airport, restaurant, shop) where students practise in role play.

questions.q: 英語日 is a day when the school —
questions.why: 英語日 (yīngyǔ rì) is a themed English day — morning broadcasts, games, signage. FETs usually help lead it.

questions.q: 晨光時間 is —
opts: the morning activity period, often run by volunteers
questions.why: 晨光時間 (chénguāng shíjiān) is the early-morning enrichment slot, frequently staffed by 愛心媽媽 volunteers.

questions.q: 愛心媽媽 are —
opts: parent volunteers who help at school
mothers on the parent committee only
teachers who run the counselling room
questions.why: 愛心媽媽 (àixīn māma) are volunteer parents who read stories, help at the gate and support morning activities.

questions.q: 社團活動 are —
questions.why: 社團活動 (shètuán huódòng) = club activities, usually one afternoon a week. Popular ones: 熱舞社, 英語社, 桌球社.

questions.q: 課後照顧 provides —
questions.why: 課後照顧 (kèhòu zhàogù) is the after-school programme running until around 5–6pm for working parents.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. You are told to ask —
questions.why: 問 (wèn) = to ask. Being redirected between 處室 (offices) is a normal part of getting anything done.

questions.q: 處室 is the collective word for —
questions.why: 處室 (chùshì) bundles 教務處, 學務處, 總務處, 輔導室 and the rest — 各處室 means 'all the offices'.

questions.q: 校長室 is the —
questions.why: 校長室 (xiàozhǎngshì) = principal's office. Visitors are often received there with tea before a school tour.

questions.q: 接待 means to —
questions.why: 接待 (jiēdài) = to receive visitors. FETs are frequently asked to help 接待 foreign guests.

questions.q: 參觀 means to —
questions.why: 參觀 (cānguān) = to tour or visit. Softer than 訪視 (fǎngshì), which is an official inspection.

questions.q: 國際交流 means international —
questions.why: 交流 (jiāoliú) = exchange. 國際交流 covers sister-school links, video calls and visiting delegations.

questions.q: A 姊妹校 is a —
questions.why: 姊妹校 (jiěmèi xiào) = sister school. Changhua schools link with schools in Japan, the US and Southeast Asia.

questions.q: 視訊交流 uses —
questions.why: 視訊 (shìxùn) = video call. 視訊交流 is the low-cost way schools run international exchange.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. You are being asked to —
questions.why: 翻譯 (fānyì) = to translate or interpret. As the FET you will be asked this often — 口譯 is interpreting, 筆譯 written translation.

questions.q: 校刊 is the school's —
questions.why: 校刊 (xiàokān) = school magazine. Teachers are often asked to contribute a short piece — a good place for an FET article.

questions.q: 投稿 means to —
questions.why: 投稿 (tóugǎo) = to submit writing. 稿子 (gǎozi) is the draft itself.

questions.q: 成果 refers to —
questions.why: 成果 (chéngguǒ) = results or achievements. 成果發表 (chéngguǒ fābiǎo) is the showcase event at the end of a programme.

questions.q: You're asked for 照片 after an event. They want —
questions.why: 照片 (zhàopiàn) = photos. Every school activity needs them for the 成果報告 and the school Facebook page.

questions.q: A form marked 待核章 is —
opts: waiting for a signature or seal
questions.why: 待 (dài) = pending. 待核章 means it still needs someone's 章 before it can move on.

questions.q: 公文流程 refers to the —
opts: routing path a document takes for approval
questions.why: 流程 (liúchéng) = process or workflow. Taiwanese 公文 travels a fixed chain: 承辦人 → 組長 → 主任 → 校長.

questions.py: zhè jiàn shì yào gēn zhǔrèn bàogào
questions.q: 🔊 Listen. This matter must be reported to the —
questions.why: 跟…報告 (gēn … bàogào) = to report to someone. 件 (jiàn) is the measure word for matters and affairs.

questions.q: 一件事 uses 件 because 件 counts —
opts: matters, affairs and items of clothing
questions.why: 件 (jiàn) counts matters and garments — 一件事 (a matter), 一件衣服 (a garment).

questions.q: 三份資料 uses 份 because 份 counts —
questions.why: 份 (fèn) counts copies and portions — 一份資料, 三十份學習單, 一份便當.

questions.q: 請給我資料 asks for —
questions.why: 資料 (zīliào) = data, materials, documents. 個人資料 (gèrén zīliào) is personal information.

questions.q: A 名單 is a —
questions.why: 名單 (míngdān) = list of names. Common in Taiwanese offices: 參加名單 (participant list), 得獎名單 (winners' list).

questions.q: 報名 means to —
questions.why: 報名 (bàomíng) = to register for something. 報名表 (bàomíngbiǎo) is the sign-up form.

questions.q: 報名截止 means registration is —
questions.why: 截止 (jiézhǐ) = to close or cut off. 截止日期 (jiézhǐ rìqí) is the deadline date.

questions.q: 活動延期 means the event has been —
questions.why: 延期 (yánqí) = to postpone. 取消 (qǔxiāo) is to cancel outright — a useful pair to keep straight.

questions.q: 取消 means to —
questions.why: 取消 (qǔxiāo) = to cancel. Typhoon days often bring 停課 (classes cancelled) announcements the night before.

questions.q: 停課 means —
questions.why: 停課 (tíngkè) = classes suspended, typically for typhoons. Check the county announcement the evening before.

questions.q: 颱風假 is a day off because of a —
questions.why: 颱風假 (táifēng jià) = typhoon day. Announced by the county government, usually around 8–10pm the night before.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. Tomorrow there will be —
questions.why: 一天 (yì tiān) = one day. 停課一天 = classes suspended for the day — the announcement everyone waits for in typhoon season.

questions.q: 補課 means —
questions.why: 補課 (bǔkè) = make-up class for one that was missed. Not the same as 補習 (bǔxí), private cram-school study.

questions.q: A 補習班 is a —
questions.why: 補習班 (bǔxíbān) = cram school. Many of your students attend one after school — worth knowing when you set homework.

questions.q: 家教 refers to —
questions.why: 家教 (jiājiào) = private tutoring. Note: FET visa conditions usually forbid outside paid work — check before agreeing.

questions.q: 我需要幫忙 tells a colleague —
questions.why: 需要 (xūyào) = to need. Asking clearly is welcomed — Taiwanese colleagues would much rather help early than fix later.

questions.q: 我可以問一下嗎？is a polite way to —
questions.why: 問一下 (wèn yíxià) = ask briefly. The 一下 softens everything — 看一下, 等一下, 幫一下.

questions.q: 確定了嗎？asks whether something is —
questions.why: 確定 (quèdìng) = certain, settled. 還沒確定 (hái méi quèdìng) means it's not fixed yet.

questions.q: 安排 means to —
questions.why: 安排 (ānpái) = to arrange. 我來安排 (wǒ lái ānpái) means 'I'll set it up'.

questions.q: 請配合 asks you to —
opts: cooperate and go along with the arrangement
questions.why: 配合 (pèihé) = to cooperate or fit in with. 請多配合 appears constantly in school notices.

questions.q: A notice ends 謝謝你的配合. It is thanking you for —
questions.why: 謝謝你的配合 = thank you for your cooperation. The standard closing line on Taiwanese school notices.
